prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Finished individual portrait for the ARC Daily Card Cabinet in the editor-approved 1950s pulp science-fiction / retro space-western direction. Authentic confident black brush outlines, painted gouache shading, fine four-color halftone and warm paper grain; vigorous saturated printed color. Every face, hand, cable and machine is drawn in ONE coherent medium. Adult naturally proportioned human features, normal-sized eyes, strong mid-century painted facial planes. NO anime, manga, chibi, giant eyes, baby face, photographic skin or photo-head collage. Source cartoon avatars establish character motifs, not verified owner human likenesses. Preserve recognizable chosen character cues while converting the illustration language. Ingenious, lightly ridiculous outsized graphics-card equipment and visible colored square ARC puzzle screens. Facial equipment physically attaches at temples/ears/cheeks with visible cabling routed into the collar and compute rig. All hardware has believable brackets, harness and weight. No scarf, cape, identical twin-GPU pillars, matching bubble-helmet uniform, medieval fantasy armor or generic neon cyber suit. Full-bleed PORTRAIT5:7, ideally1500x2100, head-through-hips; all essential headgear, hands and unique apparatus contained. Face near upper third, calmer dark lower edge usable for later overlays. NO words, letters, digits, logos, titles, speech balloons, captions, watermark, card frame or border. ONE main person only. Input1 is DZ's Son-approved community avatar: blonde hair with a short tied-back section, bangs, red/russet eyes, pale coloring, white clothing and a pink plush rabbit. Inputs2 and3 supply 1950s painted space-comic technique and adult human anatomy, not characters or poses to copy. Recast this particular chibi character as an unmistakably ADULT blonde retro-futuristic space heroine / orbital engineer with grown-up cheekbones, long naturally proportioned nose, normal-sized russet eyes, wry confident smile and restrained vintage lipstick. Preserve her blonde hair/bangs and pink rabbit motif. Fictional chosen avatar adaptation, no claimed real-life facial portrait. Dignified, energetic and capable, fully clothed practical flight equipment; no childish proportions or exaggerated pin-up anatomy.
Distinct silhouette and equipment: elegant ART-DECO RADIO CROWN built from slim layered brass circuit plates over the temples, three small vacuum-tube sensor fins at the back of the head, one circular lilac optical lens on a hinged cheek bracket, copper ear receiver, thin practical cables into a high ivory pressure collar. NO full bubble helmet and no scarf. Fitted shell-pink and ivory mechanic's flight coveralls, brushed gold buckles, burgundy utility straps and reinforced gloves. Her enormous wearable GPU is a SINGLE long chunky graphics-card cartridge mounted crosswise behind ONE shoulder, visible green PCB edges, two different-sized exposed cooling turbines, thick fluted aluminum heat sink and copper pipes. A separate big cream-and-brass CRT STAR-MAP PROJECTOR is mechanically supported on an articulated forearm brace: round glass screen displaying ONLY geometric colored ARC squares and star points, analogue amber dial, exposed vacuum tubes. One hand operates its small lever; other forearm cradles the small recognizable PINK PLUSH BUNNY from her source, secured in a snug utility sling, rabbit's little face and ears clear. Bunny is a soft toy motif, not an extra roster person. No giant twin fan pillars, jukebox instrument or radio-dish backpack. Setting: retro brass/cobalt Turducken hangar at a window above snowy GPU Valley, distant silver finned rocket and a pale lavender moon. Cream, dusty rose, burgundy, gold and cobalt print palette, charming space-queen poise mixed with a practical eccentric engineer. No other teammates, no extra animals.
